item: Row J R170: the first install reads the seeded rows back once, after the commit that created them
refs: R170; branch claude/v0-5-plan-j8zvre (PR number at push)
summary: A commit expires every row the session holds and each was re-read with its own SELECT: 13,837 of them on a first install of the shipped catalogue. seed_sources now reads the table once with populate_existing() right after a commit that created rows, and only then, so a steady boot never runs it and nothing pending can be overwritten. Measured by WAL's independent re-measure on the app's real boot (run_deferred_startup, first-install median of 6 per cell, 108 runs, one 4-CPU machine): the parent 11.28 s plain and 12.81 s encrypted, with this refresh 9.93 s and 10.55 s; statements 28,099 to 21,484; steady boots unchanged; every data table's digest identical. The first figures (10.5 s to 5.6 s) came from seedboot.py, whose default session had autoflush ON (6,862 UPDATEs the app never issues); the harness now uses the app's session options. tests/test_seed_first_install_refresh.py is red without it.
